title: Letter and Autopsy
premise: Cyrus Vasquez, the reclusive coroner of Hollow Creek, has spent a decade quietly correcting the record on deaths the town preferred to call accidents. When a drowned stranger washes up wearing clothes cut from Cyrus's own closet, the message is unmistakable: someone knows about the fourth death Cyrus never solved—the one from twenty years ago that made them an orphan and an outsider. As the anniversary dinner of the founding families approaches, Cyrus must untangle a conspiracy among the town's oldest names, discovering that their inheritance was never money but complicity. In the end, Cyrus exposes the truth at the dinner itself, chooses to stay in Hollow Creek not as its ghost but as its conscience, and finally buries the past on their own terms.
about_author: J. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent years filing death certificates in towns where everyone knew everyone's business except their own. They write mysteries about small places with long memories.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A quiet opening establishes Cyrus's ritual of speaking each name over every body they examine, and their three quiet corrections of 'accident' verdicts. The emotional beat is loneliness disguised as competence—Cyrus knows the dead better than the living know anyone.

chapters.title: Waterlogged
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A stranger's body surfaces at Miller's Bend, dressed in clothes tailored from fabric matching Cyrus's own wardrobe, down to a mended cuff only Cyrus would recognize. The beat is cold dread: this is a letter addressed personally to Cyrus.

chapters.title: What the Closet Kept
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus inventory-checks their home and finds garments missing, no signs of entry. Sheriff Dane Okonkwo dismisses it as coincidence. The beat is violated privacy—someone has been inside Cyrus's life without leaving footprints.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with flashback texture. The drowned man is identified as a private investigator hired two decades ago by the Vasquez family before the fire that killed Cyrus's parents—a case ruled accidental and sealed. The beat is old grief cracking open.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Digging into county archives, Cyrus finds the anniversary dinner of the Hollow Creek Founders' Society approaching—its twentieth iteration since the fire. Every family present then will be present now. The beat is dawning pattern recognition.

chapters.title: A Visit from Marguerite Hale
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The matriarch of the Hale family visits the morgue with condolences that feel like warnings, mentioning Cyrus's parents with suspicious precision. The beat is velvet menace; Cyrus realizes the town's kindness was always surveillance.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. An envelope arrives containing a photograph of the fire scene taken from inside the house—impossible unless the photographer was there before or during. On the back: 'Ask them what burned.' The beat is escalation from taunt to summons.

chapters.title: Ashes in the File
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The original fire report is missing pages, but the coroner's copy Cyrus inherited contains an anomaly: two sets of remains where records list one. The beat is vertigo—the closed case was never even accurately closed.

chapters.title: Dane's Debt
chapters.summary: Sheriff Okonkwo's POV. Dane privately admits his father signed off on the fire verdict under pressure from the Founders' Society, and he's spent his career paying that debt. He warns Cyrus to stop. The beat is conflicted loyalty turning toward alliance.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus tracks the PI's last known contact: Ruth Ellery, the town librarian, who has been quietly keeping clippings for twenty years. She reveals the PI found proof the fire was arson tied to a land deal. The beat is hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Land and Blood
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth explains the Vasquez property sat atop the aquifer rights the Founders' families needed; the fire cleared the claim, and orphaned Cyrus was shipped away as loose ends. The beat is righteous fury reframing Cyrus's whole exile as design.

chapters.title: Missing Pages, Missing Man
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The drowned PI had been in town a week asking questions before he died—and someone fed him Cyrus's clothing measurements. Only six people could have. The beat is paranoia narrowing into a suspect list.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus maps the six families against the old ledger and finds all six profited from the aquifer transfer. One name doesn't fit: young Theo Brandt, who inherited late and owes everyone. The beat is the trap taking shape.

chapters.title: Pressure Crack
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, terrified, nearly confesses to Cyrus that he was paid to rent the PI a room and look away—but stops short when Marguerite appears behind him in the diner. The beat is fear as a leash; the reader sees the machinery up close.

chapters.title: Exhumation
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Using the two-sets-of-remains anomaly, Cyrus legally forces exhumation of the fire victims' plot. The second set of remains is not a Vasquez—it belongs to the Founders' Society's long-lost treasurer. The beat is the past physically refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Threats in the Dark
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus's office is ransacked, evidence samples destroyed, and Ruth is hospitalized in a staged fall. The message: stop, or become the next accident. The beat is grief hardening into resolve—Cyrus stops being careful.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Buried
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite reflects on the night of the fire: her husband killed the treasurer who tried to stop the arson, and she has spent twenty years curating the lie. The beat is chilling self-justification—she believes she protected the town.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus receives a formal invitation to the anniversary dinner in their parents' honor—an obvious stage for a final silencing. Dane offers to arrest Marguerite on thin evidence; Cyrus refuses, wanting the whole truth in the open. The beat is deliberate walk into danger.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the dinner, Cyrus stands, presents the exhumation findings, the land ledger, and the tailor's receipt linking the stolen clothes to Marguerite's household. Marguerite counters smoothly—until Theo, freed by Ruth's survival, corroborates everything. The beat is public detonation.

chapters.title: Confession at the Table
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Cornered before the entire town, Marguerite delivers a cold, complete confession, naming her husband posthumously and daring the town to pretend again. Dane arrests her as the Founders watch their myth collapse. The beat is catharsis through unflinching truth.

chapters.title: Correcting the Record
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Weeks later, Cyrus amends four death certificates—including their parents'—and speaks each name aloud over the reopened files. The town is raw, divided, but finally honest. The beat is mourning completed at last, grief given paperwork and dignity.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus tends their parents' restored headstone, plants spring bulbs, and accepts the town's awkward new warmth—not forgiveness, but belonging earned through truth. A final line echoes the first chapter's ritual. The beat is quiet resolution: Cyrus stays, visible at last.
